rappel_detail.notes: First rappel from the top; plan on at least two ropes given the sustained overhanging terrain.
hazards: the wall overhangs enough on many pitches that the next station is not below you - plan on swinging in or leaving directional gear on nearly every rappel, and expect a free hang if you miss

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 16, one per pitch, from the bolted anchor at the top of pitch 15.
Rappel 3 of 16, one per pitch, from the bolted anchor at the top of pitch 14.
Rappel 4 of 16, one per pitch, from the bolted anchor at the top of pitch 13.
Rappel 5 of 16, one per pitch, from the bolted anchor at the top of pitch 12.
Rappel 6 of 16, one per pitch, from the bolted anchor at the top of pitch 11.
Covers the pitch that overhangs 40+ feet; this section requires either fixed lines or down-aiding to manage the roof.
hazards: the biggest overhang on the route - rappelling it clean without a fixed line strands you off the wall
rappel_detail.station: This is the pitch that overhangs 40-plus feet. Without a line fixed on the way up you have to down-aid a long way to stay on the wall and reach the next station; a 40 m line is reported to be long enough to fix here.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 8 of 16, one per pitch, from the bolted anchor at the top of pitch 9.
Roughly the midpoint of the wall; the FA party's long haul-bag-rider rappel spanned part of this middle section.

hazards: arriving at the gear belay and looking for bolts that are not there is the trap on this station
rappel_detail.station: Pitch 15 is the one pitch without a bolted belay - the belay is gear, on a large ledge. The bolted rappel anchor is set far to the right along that ledge as you face the wall, not at the belay, so walk the ledge to find it.

rappel_detail.pull: Strip any lines fixed during the ascent on the way down; leaving them is discouraged here and the buttress already carries old rope from previous attempts that should not be trusted.
rappel_detail.notes: Final rappel to the base; remove any fixed lines left during the ascent as an established leave-no-trace practice on this route.

set.rappel_count_note: Rappel the route, one rappel per pitch: every pitch has a bolted stainless-steel anchor except pitch 15, whose gear belay has a bolted rappel anchor along the ledge to the right. Pitch lengths are not published, so no rappel lengths are given; bring two ropes. Much of the wall overhangs, so plan on directional pieces or swinging in to reach stations, and on fixing or down-aiding pitch 7. The first-ascent party descended unconventionally, one climber riding the haul bags down roughly 1,000-1,200 ft before the rest finished with double-rope rappels, which is not a plan for a repeat.
